---
title: "Testing"
---


447 tests, all of which run without a Zotero installation and without network
access.

```sh
uv sync --extra vega --group dev
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check src tests scripts
uv run mypy
```

## Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the suite on every Python version the
classifiers claim — 3.11 through 3.14 on Linux, plus 3.13 on macOS, because
the plotting stack is the part most likely to differ between platforms. A
version listed in the metadata but never exercised is a claim, not a fact.

Four further jobs: `ruff` and `mypy` and a documentation build; the quality
snapshot against its committed baseline; a wheel and sdist through
`twine check`; and the cross-language congruence job described below.

::: {.callout-warning title="Three tests skip in an ordinary checkout"}

The comparisons that assert a frozen reference is byte-identical to the
copy in [qdaR](https://qdar.zotqda.org) need the R package **beside** this one on disk. In a bare
clone they skip, and a skipped test proves nothing while looking like it
passed.

The `congruence` job therefore checks out both repositories side by side,
runs those tests, and **fails if any of them skips anyway** — a guard
against the day someone moves the reference file and the skip silently
becomes permanent. It is switched on by the repository variable
`QDAR_PUBLISHED`, so it stays off until the R package has a public
repository to check out rather than failing for a reason that is not a
defect.

Locally the tests find qdaR whenever the two packages sit in the same
parent directory, which is how the development tree is laid out.
:::

## What the suite is actually for

Most of it is ordinary: readers reject malformed files, coefficients match
hand computations, figures build. Two parts are unusual and are the reason the
numbers here can be trusted.

### Congruence with the plugin

`test/qdaz-reference.json` holds 109 randomly generated coder matrices, two
to four coders, deliberately skewed marginals, missing ratings, together with
the values the plugin's JavaScript computes for them. `test_congruence.py`
recomputes all six coefficients and compares to twelve decimal places.

That file is byte-identical to the one in the R package, and one test asserts
exactly that. So three implementations in three languages are held to a single
reference rather than to each other.

Agreeing on a hand-picked example proves very little. The fixtures were
generated at random precisely so that no one chose them to make the
implementations agree.

### Congruence with the R twin on the statistics

`tests/stats-reference.json` holds what qdaR computes for
`test/stats-fixture.csv` — 256 codings over six codes, five documents and two
coders, with expected counts small enough to force the exact-test branch.
`test_stats.py` reproduces the chi-squared statistic, Cramér's V, the Jaccard
matrix, the cophenetic correlation, the scaling distances and the
correspondence-analysis inertias.

The two packages compute all of this through entirely different libraries —
R's `chisq.test`, `cmdscale`, `hclust` and `MASS::corresp` against scipy and
hand-written linear algebra, so agreement to twelve decimals is evidence
about the statistics, not about shared code.

Two of the comparisons cannot be literal. Scaling coordinates and
correspondence scores are defined only up to sign and rotation, so what gets
compared is the pairwise distances between points, which are invariant under
both. The Monte Carlo p-value is random by construction on either side, so it
only has to land close.

### Congruence on the newer measures

Two further frozen references work the same way. `qdaz-e35-reference.json`
covers the unitizing alpha, WindowDiff, Pk, the saturation ratio and the
Wilson interval; `qdaz-gamma-reference.json` covers gamma. Both were computed
by the plugin's JavaScript on randomly generated data and are byte-identical
to the copies in the sibling package, which a test asserts.

Some of these numbers were also checked against the papers themselves rather
than only against each other. The unitizing alpha reproduces the observed
disagreement of 7.8 from Krippendorff's own worked example; the sample-size
functions reproduce Donner and Rotondi's Table 2 in all forty-eight cells and
Fugard and Potts' Table 1 cell for cell; gamma reproduces the three
configurations of Mathet and colleagues' Figure 11, including the negative
value for coders who do worse than chance.

That combination matters. Agreement between three implementations proves they
are consistent; agreement with a published table proves they are right.

## Regenerating a reference

Do this only when a coefficient has legitimately changed on one side, never to
make a failing test pass.

Generate the fixtures once, in whichever language is convenient. Feed them to
the plugin's `src/stats.js` under Node, which takes a `global.QdaZ = {}` and an
`eval` of the file, and to this package. Then compare, and resolve every single
difference before going any further; a reference frozen while two
implementations disagree is worse than no reference. Only then write the new
JSON, into **both** packages, in the same commit.

When picking which fixtures to freeze, make sure the selection covers every
coder count **and** matrices with missing ratings. A regular stride such as
`seq(1, n, by = 4)` once happened to miss every single gap, and the coverage
test in `test_congruence.py` exists to catch exactly that.

## Verifying that a test can fail

A test that has never failed is a claim, not a check. Both congruence tests
were verified by mutation: perturbing the pooled chance term in `fleiss()` by
one part in a million makes 108 of 112 cases fail. If you touch these
computations, do the same before trusting the green tick.

## Testing against the built distribution

Passing in the source tree does not prove the reference files resolve from an
installed package:

```sh
python -m build
pip install "dist/qdapy-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl[vega]"
cd /tmp && python -m pytest <path>/tests
```

Both `importlib.resources` lookups and the `qdapy.example()` paths only get
exercised properly this way.
